senses.gloss:
Khajurāho
------------------------------------------
India is a land of temples. The Candella dynasty which ruled over Jejaka-bhukti—the present day Bundelkhand of Madhya Pradesh—from the 9th to the 14th centuries, has left a large number of beautiful temples built around A. D. 1000 which are situated near खजुराहो, a village close to Chatarpur, about 45 kms. (28 miles) from it. These temples belong not only to the Hindu cults of शैविस्म् and वैष्णविस्म् but also to जैनिस्म्.
महादेव Temple">Kandariya महादेव TempleThe हिन्दु तेम्प्लेस् are in two rows. The largest and the best of these is the कन्दरिय महादेव तेम्प्ले of Lord शिव. It is built on a platform which is 8.6 metres (28.5 ft.) above the ground level. The temple itself is 32.7 metres (109 ft.) long and 18 metres (60 ft.) wide. The height of the gopuram is 35 metres (116 ft.) above the ground level. An important characteristic of this temple is a duplication of the vimānas from the flat roof of the mukhamaṇṭapa (entrance) on all sides until the central and real roof of the main shrine is reached. Each succeeding विमान is bigger than the preceding one. The final विमान is akin to that of the Liṅgarāja temple of Bhubaneśvar in Orissa.
The विष्णु temple is 25 1/2 metres (85 ft.) by 13 metres (44 ft.). Based on the pañcāyatana principle, it has five shrines. The image of विष्णु with four arms is very beautiful.
Generally, all the temples have one entrance, gradually leading to ardha-maṇṭapa, main maṇṭapa (or hall), अन्तराल and then the गर्भगृह (sanctum). There is also a passage round the main sanctum for pradakṣiṇā or circumambulation.
The Kandariya महादेव or the शिव temple has a very large number of erotic sculptures on the outside, in various postures, which is rather intriguing.
There are also six Jain temples usually 18 metres (60 ft.) by 9 metres (30 ft.). They are simpler in structure though beautiful.
